o: We must order all blocks into a sequence starting from the ground (height 0), burning (difference)^2 per hop, and maximize the total. For [1,7,9] the order 9,1,7 burns 81+64+36=181; for [5,2,4] the order 5,2,4 burns 25+9+4=38. Because squaring is convex, large gaps are disproportionately valuable, so the optimal tour repeatedly alternates between the largest and smallest remaining values - a 'pendulum' order over the sorted array, beginning with the maximum (which also maximizes the initial jump from height 0).
k: Convexity of x^2 means the total is maximized by making individual jumps as extreme as possible.
After sorting, visiting max, min, second max, second min, ... (pendulum order) maximizes the sum of squared consecutive gaps.
Starting with the global maximum simultaneously optimizes the first jump from the ground.

a.i: Sort the heights, then emit them alternating from the top and bottom of the remaining range, starting with the maximum. An exchange argument shows any other order can be rearranged to increase (or keep) every squared gap, so this local-extremal tour is globally optimal.
s: Build the visit order by alternately taking the current largest then smallest remaining element, starting with the largest.
Simulate the jumps from height 0 through this order, accumulating squared differences.
a.t: O(n log n) - dominated by sorting; the tour construction and summation are linear
a.sp: O(n) for the sorted copy and visit order

w: Lead with the convexity intuition, then the pendulum construction; verify against both provided examples live. Pitfalls: forgetting the first jump starts from height 0 (not from another block), using 32-bit accumulation (values reach ~1e10 in Java/C++), and assuming simply 'sort ascending' works (it fails on example 2). Follow-up: minimize calories instead, or allow skipping one block.
